subject: psychology
title: Model Question Paper 2
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 100 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Section A: questions 1–20 are MCQs (1 mark each); questions 21–29 carry 2 marks (two parts of 1 mark each) and questions 30–32 carry 4 marks (four parts of 1 mark each).
Section B: questions 33–38 carry 2 marks (30–50 words), questions 39–44 carry 3 marks (50–80 words) and questions 45–48 carry 5 marks (80–120 words).
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: Unstructured interview consists of ______ questions. A case study studies one ______.
(i) What is an aptitude? (ii) What is meant by aptitude battery?
questions.answer: (i) A combination of characteristics indicating a person's capacity to acquire a specific skill or knowledge after training. (ii) A set of aptitude tests developed to assess several aptitudes, e.g. DAT and GATB.

questions.q: Name: (i) the scientist who advocated operant conditioning; (ii) the apparatus he used.
Name the two types of depth cues.
Name any two social motives.
questions.answer: Achievement, affiliation, power, nurturance, aggression, exploration (any two).

questions.q: Fill in: (i) A child liked by some and disliked by others is called ______. (ii) An internal determiner of emotional development is ______.
Fill in: (i) The gland that controls adolescent growth is the ______. (ii) The primary sign of maturity in girls is ______.
Differentiate density and crowding in one line each.
questions.answer: Density is the objective number of persons per unit area; crowding is the subjective feeling of discomfort.

questions.q: What is the Psychic being according to Sri Aurobindo?
questions.answer: The innermost core of the being, a spark of the Divine, also called Atman.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is meant by random assignment?
questions.answer: Every participant has an equal chance of being in the experimental or control condition, removing systematic differences between groups.

questions.q: What is sensation?
questions.answer: The process by which sensory neurons convert energy such as light into neural impulses, giving awareness of conditions inside or outside the body.

questions.q: What is meant by asynchronization of development?
questions.answer: Skeletal and muscular growth is faster than learning to use the new muscle mass, so the body needs new learning.

questions.q: How do peers shape attitudes?
questions.answer: We adopt the group's attitudes, and praise and approval from friends reward and strengthen them (instrumental learning).

questions.q: What is ability?
questions.answer: The innate capacity to act that helps in solving a problem; environment can develop it but cannot produce it.

questions.q: Differentiate mind and intellect.
questions.answer: Mind receives stimuli and stores memories and emotions; the intellect discriminates, judges and takes rational decisions.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: What is survey method? Where can you use the survey method?
questions.answer: Survey is a research method in which people's opinions are collected on current issues through questionnaires, interviews, email or SMS. It is used to study the pattern of opinions, attitudes, beliefs and values, to test hypotheses about variables (e.g. after the Mumbai attacks) and for opinion polls in elections, in psychology, sociology, political science and management.

or.q: What are the different methods of data collection for research? Explain any three.
or.answer: Observation (studying behaviour as it occurs, naturalistic or laboratory), experiment (manipulating the independent variable), case study (detailed profile of an individual), survey (opinions through questionnaire or interview) and psychological tests.

questions.q: Describe the problem with eyewitness testimony.
questions.answer: Eyewitness errors in perception are common, especially when the person is surprised, stressed or threatened; hence investigators and jurors should gather more evidence than rely only on eyewitnesses.

questions.q: Explain the characteristics of motivation.
questions.answer: Motivation pushes us to goals and needs optimum arousal; it is influenced by pleasing external stimuli such as money and food; it results from thoughts and expectations and may be intrinsic or extrinsic; and needs are ordered, basic needs first.

questions.q: Describe the characteristics of middle adulthood.
questions.answer: Competence, maturity, responsibility and stability; attention on health, children and ageing parents and plans for old age; menopause in women; creativity; generativity versus self-absorption; turbulence from awareness of mortality.

questions.q: Explain the types of conflict with examples.
questions.answer: Approach–approach between two desirable goals; avoidance–avoidance between two undesirable goals; approach–avoidance with attraction and fear of the same goal.

questions.q: Explain leadership styles and their effect.
questions.answer: Authoritarian, paternalistic, consultative and participative. The more participative the boss, the greater the productivity and satisfaction and the lower the absenteeism and turnover.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain aptitude and interest and how they are assessed.
questions.answer: Aptitude is the capacity to acquire a specific skill after training; it differs from intelligence and achievement. Aptitude tests (clerical, mechanical, musical, typing) predict vocational success; batteries are DAT, GATB and ASVAB. Interest is measured by vocational interest tests (paper-pencil tests matching interest with occupations) and general interest inventories.

questions.q: Explain the barriers and the features of effective communication.
questions.answer: Barriers: distortion, selective perception, projection, overload, emotions and differing word meanings. Effective communication needs a common frame of reference, mutual interest, common language and common environment, plus tips: voice modulation, thinking before speaking, appropriate distance and culturally sensitive signs.

questions.q: Describe the strategies for time management.
questions.answer: Make an activity schedule with a list prepared the night before, prioritise tough tasks first, identify uninterrupted periods, be flexible, set aside time for exercise and yoga and plan leisure such as music or gardening.

questions.q: Explain any one model of human–environment relationship and the concept of environmental stress.
questions.answer: Environmental stress is an undesirable person–environment transaction. In the symbiotic model, humans and nature are interdependent; blind exploitation of resources like oil and coal causes pollution and threats, so balance and duty to nature are needed.
